title: Rapid Decision Studio — Facilitation Notes & Slide Outline
body:
Purpose:
Quick facilitation guide + slide skeleton for a 3-hour customer "Decision Studio" used to converge on a single recommended inference architecture for a reference POC. The goal is to leave with: (1) chosen model family + quantization plan, (2) target latency/throughput SLOs, (3) roadmap of engineering tasks with owners for the POC.

Context and audience:
- Customer: mid-market SaaS company with search and summarization features; security-sensitive (SaaS + SOC2 in scope).
- Attendees: customer PM, 2 product engineers, 1 infra lead, 4 Redwood attendees (SE lead, runtime engineer, SRE, product manager).
- Pre-reads: short usage traces and current latency graphs (ask customer to provide 24-48 hour token distribution).

High-level agenda (3 hrs) — timeboxed:
1) 0:00–0:15 — Welcome, goals, and rules of engagement (facilitator)
   - Quick intros + role call (who decides, who can block)
   - Define success criteria for this session (must-haves vs nice-to-haves)
2) 0:15–0:35 — Customer context & workload profile (customer PM + engineer)
   - Present 2 minute high-level product flow, 5 minute request/volume profile, 5 minute cost/ops sensitivities
3) 0:35–1:00 — Constraint mapping exercise (team split into two breakout groups)
   - Map: latency SLO, peak qps, security constraints, data residency, budget envelope
   - Output: top 3 constraints per group (stickies to shared board)
4) 1:00–1:25 — Model candidate quick review (Redwood presents 3 candidates)
   - For each: perf profile, quantization options, expected cost delta, fallback plan
5) 1:25–1:40 — Break and live demo prep (runtime engineer sets up short demo endpoint)
6) 1:40–2:10 — Live sampling & quality checks (run 6 canonical prompts with each candidate)
   - Vote on quality: accept / marginal / reject (anonymous polling)
7) 2:10–2:40 — Routing & fallback design (architected by SRE + SE)
   - Discuss batching policies, cache strategy, graceful degradation approach
8) 2:40–2:55 — Decision rubric and commit (capture chosen option and tradeoffs)
   - Write one-line recommendation + 3 risks and mitigations
9) 2:55–3:00 — Next steps and owners (PM to confirm timeline)

Slide outline (20–25 slides, speaker notes):
1 Title slide — Rapid Decision Studio: [Customer name] POC
2 Session goals + success criteria (explicit: min deliverables)
3 Attendees and decision roles (RACI-lite)
4 Current product flow diagram (customer to present)
5 Usage profile snapshot (tokens, qps, peak hours)
6 Constraint map (visual of prioritized constraints)
7 Candidate model matrix (rows: model, quant, latency, cost, fallback)
8 Candidate A details (perf chart + sample outputs)
9 Candidate B details (perf chart + sample outputs)
10 Candidate C details (perf chart + sample outputs)
11 Demo plan and commands (engineer notes)
12 Live sample results table (show side-by-side outputs)
13 Voting heatmap (quality votes)
14 Batching + cache recommendation (settings and rationale)
15 Deployment topology options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
16 Fallback and graceful degradation playbook
17 Security and compliance considerations (KMS, VPC, audit)
18 Risk register (top 5 risks + mitigations)
19 Implementation milestones (30 / 60 / 90-day plan)
20 Owner matrix with tickets (link to JIRA backlog)
21 Cost projection (tokens / infra estimate)
22 Acceptance criteria for POC
23 Support and escalation path (SRE contacts, SLAs)
24 Appendix: perf measurement details and test harness
25 Appendix: glossary and reference artifacts

Facilitation notes & tactics (tips to run a smooth session):
- Start by setting a clear decision authority: name the person who has final sign-off at the top. Call them out early.
- Use short anchoring statements: every 10 minutes, state current decision state (e.g., "we're leaning B for quality, but A for cost").
- Keep live demos tiny: 3 canonical prompts chosen before the session. Avoid ad-hoc tests that extend time.
- During voting, use silent numeric polling (post-it or poll) to avoid bias by loud voices.
- If disagreement stalls, fall back to two-step tie-breaker: (1) quality threshold filter then (2) cost/ops tie-breaker.
- Timebox open technical debates to 10 minutes; capture unresolved items as "parking-lot" and assign owner.

Prep checklist for Redwood SEs (pre-session):
- Gather customer's 48h token distribution and sample prompts.
- Pre-compute approximate latency/cost for 3 candidate configs (p99, median, cost/token).
- Stand up short-lived demo endpoints (three) in staging + smoke test.
- Create slide deck skeleton and share 24hrs prior.
- Create voting poll and shared board (Miro or Jamboard).

Roles and responsibilities during session:
- Facilitator (SE lead): time, decisions, parking-lot owner.
- Runtime engineer: demo, perf numbers, on-call for infra issues.
- SRE: deployment topology and reliability constraints.
- Product manager (Redwood): capture acceptance criteria and next steps.
- Customer decision maker: final sign-off and budget confirmation.
- Recorder: meeting notes + action items (send within 24hrs).

Decision capture template (one-line fields):
- Chosen model and variant:
- Quantization profile:
- Target SLOs (latency p50/p90/p99, throughput):
- POC success metrics (quality metric + cost threshold):
- Top 3 risks and mitigations:
- Next milestone and owner:

Follow-ups (post-session):
- Send final deck + decision capture within 24hrs (Recorder)
- Create JIRA epics and tasks for infra, runtime, and eval (SE lead)
- Schedule 2-week check-in and 60-day review (PM)

Common pitfalls and mitigation notes:
- Pitfall: customer pushes for cheapest option without quality baseline. Mitigation: require quality vote with clear pass/fail rule.
- Pitfall: long live demos kill time. Mitigation: strict 3-prompt demo and pre-registered inputs.
- Pitfall: unclear ownership for infra tasks. Mitigation: assign owners before leaving meeting and create tickets immediately.

Open questions to get from customer before session:
- Provide 48h request traces and token length distribution?
- What's the internal approval timeline for infra spend?
- Any regulatory constraints (EU data residency, HIPAA) we must consider?

Sticky notes / raw facilitator thoughts (notes to self):
- If SLOs unrealistic, propose canary with lower traffic and defined rollback triggers.
- Keep cost figures as ranges, not absolutes — customers tend to fixate on single number.
- Use concrete examples for fallbacks: e.g., degrade to 1-shot summarization with caching rather than full model downgrade.

Appendix: quick checklist for demo commands (for runtime engineer):
- Warm up KV cache by sending small batches before live run.
- Run 3 canonical prompts x 3 models, capture p95 latency and token counts.
- Screenshot all runs and export raw text for voting.

End of document.
